pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — TERMLY EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

2. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.

3. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

5. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.

6. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

7. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

8. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.

9. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. happiness

10. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

11. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

12. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

13. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

14. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

15. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language School.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

4. C — Where is the library?

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

9. A — run

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

13. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

14. C — went

15. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Language Welcome and; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
